questions.title: "What exactly does "warp-specialization" mean in FlashAttention‑3 and how does it improve asynchronous execution?
questions.question_body: The paper says that FlashAttention‑3 uses warp-specialisation to split producer warps and consumer warps while enabling TMA loads and WGMMA multiplies to run asynchronously. I am still unsure what constraints are enforced when a warp becomes a producer versus a consumer and how this split hides load latency versus computation latency.

questions.title: "How does FlashAttention‑3 perform row-wise softmax without materialising the whole score matrix S ?
questions.question_body:
"The algorithm refers to a “local” softmax reduction over blocks shown in Alg. 1–end lines 14–20.
I would like a clearer step-by-step description of how this block-wise reduction ensures that the final probabilities match those obtained by assembling all $S_{ij}$ tiles into a full $N	imes N$ matrix before computing $	ext{softmax}(S)$.

questions.title: "Why must FP8 WGMMA operands satisfy a k-major layout while FP16 allows both mn-major and k-major layouts?
questions.question_body:
"Section 2.2 mentions that WGMMA for fp8 only accepts operands whose inner dimension $k$ is contiguous.
Could you explain why this requirement exists at >hardware> or PTX>level and what would go wrong if I attempted an mn-major operand with fp8 tensors?

questions.title: "Can you walk through Intuition behind the two-stage GEMM‑softmax pipeline used by the consumer warpgroup
questions.question_body:
"Alg. 2 shows variables $	ext{S}_{	ext{cur}}$, $	ext{S}_{	ext{next}}$, $	ilde{	ext{P}}_{	ext{cur}}$, $m_i$.
I’d appreciate an annotated walk-through showing exactly which instructions overlap (e.g., which WMMA commit locks release), why we need two stages instead of one, and how register pressure grows during this overlap.

questions.title: "What is ‘ping‑pong scheduling’ between warpgroups and how does it help hide softmax latency?
questions.question_body:
"Figure 4 describes lane-swapped execution where GCMP groups alternate giving rise to overall better utilisation.
I’m unclear about which CUDA events/barriers enable this alternating behaviour – specifically which lines correspond to waiting for one group’s WGMMAs while another executes separate softmax logic.

questions.title: "How does block quantization reduce numerical errors compared with per-tensor scaling when applying FP8 precision?
questions.question_body:
"Section 2 deals with outlier activations present in LLMs.
I understand per-tensor scaling applies one global scalar per matrix.
Could you illustrate formally why applying one scalar per block eases exponent variations across elements so arithmetic errors shrink?

questions.title: "Why perform an ‘in-kernel” transpose on V tiles instead of pre-transposing globally before running fp8 attention?
questions.question_body:
"The discussion explains that TMA loads cannot change stride direction.
When $V$ tiles come into SMEM they must become k-major, yet doing an off-chip transpose would cost bandwidth.
Could you detail why doing LDSM–STSM transposes in register space during kernel launch actually beats any off-chip pre-processing?

questions.title: "Incoherent processing via random orthogonal matrix M preserves attention outputs yet improves quantisation – why?
questions.question_body:
"Equation (∗) claims $(Q M)(K M)^{	op} = QK^{	op}$ when $M$ is orthogonal.
Beyond this algebraic identity also reduces distortion from fp8 rounding.
Please explain intuitively how multiplying both Q and K by $M$ spreads large values across dimensions so that subsequent per-block scalers capture better statistics.

questions.title: "Which exact operations store data at fp32 versus fp16/fp8 during FlashAttention‑3’s forward pass?
questions.question_body:
"The paper asserts intermediates such as $	ilde{P}$ are kept in higher precision.
Can you enumerate the sequence – e.g., SS-GEMM produces an fp32 accumulator cast down to fp16/8 before exponentiation – so i know when accuracy preservation catches up versus speed envelopes?

questions.title: "How is peak TFLOPs/s measured on an H100 GPU to report a pathological point such as ‘up to 740 TFLOPs/s reaching 75 % utilisation’?
questions.question_body:
"Section 4 gives absolute speeds but doesn’t describe how these figures derive from hardware specs.
Could you elaborate on computing theoretical peak FLOPs based on tensor-core count, clock‐rate and instruction throughput plus the folding factor used during our benchmark kernels?
